correctness.rationale: The pair of parametrized parabolas has dot product st+ab s²t², exactly the displayed M. Over O=Z_p[ζ_p], the p−1 Fourier character table is invertible since p−1 is a unit; the nonzero-coordinate matrix becomes a 2×2 origin/trivial block with determinant Δ_c=Σ_{u≠0}(ζ^{u+c u²}−1) and a monomial diagonal of L_r(c)=Σ_{u≠0}ω(u)^r ζ^{u+c u²}. For E=p−1−r, the first nonzero binomial jet of L_r is at k=ceil(E/2), and its coefficient ±c^floor(E/2)/(floor(E/2)!) (or c^k/k!) is nonzero mod p for c≠0. Lower coefficients divisible by p carry valuation ≥p−1>k, preventing cancellation. For Δ_c, the first nonzero jet is at m=(p−1)/2 and a unit c^m/m!, while constant term vanishes; hence vπ(Δ_c)=m. The resulting complete curved sequence is 0,1,1,...,m,m. When c=0, an integral unitriangular monomial-to-Newton basis change of the p×p Fourier matrix and π^k-divisibility by column give diagonal exact valuations 0,...,p−1. The sums yield determinant valuations (p²−1)/4 and p(p−1)/2, nonsingularity and exact maximum inverse denominator exponents.
